A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DCT-CryptoNets work. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices support comparison, including matching material across appendix reordering.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification accuracies, encrypted-inference simulations, latency measurements, operation counts and ablation results in Section 4 and Appendix A.

after.justification: v2 retains the original empirical results, including dataset comparisons and quantization, ReLU-pruning and cryptographic-hyperparameter ablations.

M1.justification: Both retain the DCT preprocessing, modified ResNet architectures, first-layer ReLU pruning, quantization-aware training and TFHE programmable bootstrapping. The expanded key-handling explanation documents deployment without establishing a changed inference procedure.

E1.justification: Both use CIFAR-10, mini-ImageNet, Imagenette and ImageNet, with the same image-resolution and frequency-channel scenarios. The new threat-model discussion does not introduce an evaluated security task.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Table 4 and the appendix comparisons. CryptoDL becoming Hesamifard et al. (2017), Faster Cryptonets becoming Chou et al. (2018), and the updated Lee citations are naming changes, not new baselines.

E3.justification: The matched evaluation procedures remain the same, but new v2 Table 8 lists 4-bit ImageNet weights and activations while Section 3.2 still specifies 5-bit quantization in both versions. The PDFs do not resolve whether this is a setting revision or a documentation error. Other newly listed training settings are disclosures rather than established protocol changes.

E4.justification: The frequency-selection, resolution, ReLU-pruning, quantization and cryptographic-hyperparameter analyses are retained. v1 Appendices A.1–A.4 correspond to v2 A.5, A.3, A.4 and A.6. The new security discussion supplies no attack experiments or robustness tests.

E5.justification: Section 4.2 retains the same 95% bootstrap confidence intervals, using 10,000 repetitions over combinations of 20 subsets containing 200 random images each. No seed, repeated-run or statistical-estimation practice changes are reported.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4 retain their result entries; for example, Table 4 reports ImageNet DCT ResNet-18 accuracy of 66.3% and latency of 8,562 seconds in both versions. v1 Tables 5–8 match v2 Tables 6, 5, 7 and 9 without numerical changes. New Table 8 contains settings, not outcomes.

T1.justification: The TFHE algebra, DCT equation and PBS error model remain unchanged. v2 omits the elementary dequantization restatement from Section 2.4 but does not revise the mathematical framework. The new security discussion introduces no formal proof or mathematical security model.

C1.justification: Both claim reduced encrypted computation, up to 5.3× speedup, improved encrypted-accuracy reliability and better scaling with image resolution. The isolated 1.7×–2.4× DCT speedup emphasized in v2 Section 4.3 already appeared in v1's conclusion.

C2.justification: New Appendix A.1 qualifies deployment security by distinguishing honest-but-curious and malicious servers, discussing possible verifiable computation, and identifying client-device and secret-key dependencies. Existing interpretations of accuracy, bootstrapping costs and small-image limitations remain largely unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 substantially expands reproducibility information through a project-code link and release statement, Table 8's training schedules, batch sizes, optimizer settings and quantizer classes, and Appendix A.2's secret/evaluation-key workflow. However, v1's augmentation list and 4:2:2 channel-selection disclosure are omitted, and the new ImageNet bit-width information is inconsistent.

R1.justification: v2 adds references on JPEG-domain learning, ENSEI, foundational TFHE and verifiable FHE/security. Section 2.5 more explicitly distinguishes learning frequency-domain features from frequency-domain convolution techniques. These additions refine the existing positioning without redefining the contribution.

P1.justification: The abstract, methodological overview and conclusion are revised, with explanatory edits elsewhere while retaining the main section sequence and much of the prose. The appendix is reordered and gains a contents list; a reproducibility statement and expanded acknowledgements are added.

P2.justification: v2 adopts ICLR formatting, simplifies Figure 2 by removing the intermediate DCT-Net column, adds RGB/DCT grouping to Table 1 and introduces hyperparameter Table 8. Existing figures and tables are relocated or resized, including Figures 3 and 4 exchanging numbers; most result displays retain their structure.

improvement.justification: The training details, code-access pointer and clearer deployment/security discussion make v2 more useful for understanding and reproducing the unchanged work. These gains are tempered by Table 8's ImageNet bit-width conflict with Section 3.2 and the loss of augmentation and channel-selection details. The net improvement is useful but limited.
